name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district (D+13 partisan lean) with an incumbent running
Grijalva holds a large fundraising edge ($2.3M raised, $428K on hand vs. $224K and $11K for Butierez)
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96% to win
No public general-election polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to the Democrat: a D+13 district, an incumbent with a roughly ten-to-one cash advantage, and markets pricing her near-certain to win. With no polling to contradict that picture, the race stays in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much narrower margin, or a surge of outside spending against Grijalva, would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adelita Grijalva, the Democratic incumbent in Arizona's 7th District, is running for a full term in a seat her party holds by a wide margin. The district's partisan lean of D+13 gives Republicans little structural opening, and Grijalva enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage: she has raised about $2.3 million and holds $428,000 on hand, while Republican Daniel Butierez has raised roughly $224,000 with under $12,000 available. Outside spending has been minimal and mostly on her side.

Prediction markets put the Democratic side's win probability near 96 percent, and no public general-election polls or expert ratings complicate that picture. The forecast treats the seat as Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any evidence of a competitive race.
